statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of four representative public archetypes and preference/mobile/failure conditions.

page.framework: React-based client application with server metadata/detail content
page.notes: Public visual-discovery service. Homepage, Explore listing, board detail, login flow and missing-route recovery were sampled. Authenticated feed, pin creation, account settings, checkout/ads tooling and post-login personalisation were not covered because no account credentials were provided.

paths.description: Public homepage/landing archetype: purpose, discovery entry, consent, preferences, mobile layout, performance, security and network.
Explore/listing archetype: category discovery and unauthenticated access wall.
Board/detail content archetype: rich entity metadata, content rendering and crawler visibility.
Primary account-flow archetype: labels, autocomplete, empty submission, recovery and auth options.
Failure/recovery path using a deliberately nonexistent route.

findings.summary: The public experience ignores the system dark-colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white/light-grey surface and the DOM reports color-scheme: normal under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, image-overlay and dialog tokens.

findings.summary: Major state changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: The interaction video shows the consent layer disappearing and content changing without a directional or continuity cue; no active View Transition was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for major modal/state changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The site chrome does not communicate scroll state.
findings.evidence: The interaction video shows a long content page with no progress or scroll-state response in its navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a lightweight progress affordance for long discovery surfaces.

findings.summary: Load-time overlays repeatedly obscure the primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop, Explore and login captures all open with a viewport-dimming consent or login layer over the content; Explore is blocked by login before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep public exploration usable before sign-in, defer non-essential prompts, and preserve an immediate, obvious dismiss path.

findings.summary: The cookie modal is an ad-hoc ARIA dialog rather than the platform dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: The document probe finds a DIV role=dialog aria-modal=true; no <dialog> is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, showModal(), close(), focus restoration, Escape handling and a non-modal fallback where appropriate.

findings.summary: The mobile homepage is horizontally clipped and unusable.
findings.evidence: At 360x800, layout reports scrollWidth 929 versus visual viewport 360, 569 px overflow; the screenshot clips headings and most of the consent dialog off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove desktop minimum widths, size overlays with max-inline-size/min(), and verify intrinsic reflow at 320-400 CSS px.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target treatment are insufficient.
findings.evidence: The focused skip link computes outline:none and box-shadow:none; Lighthouse fails target-size for the Pinterest app controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and ensure unobscured targets have at least 24x24 CSS px safe space, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Failure and recovery states are misleading or absent.
findings.evidence: A nonexistent URL renders the normal homepage rather than a clear 404/recovery state, while HAR records two 404 API calls and Lighthouse logs them as console errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 page/status with useful navigation, and expose actionable inline retry/error states for failed data calls.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are far outside good thresholds.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 18.4 s, CLS 0.463 and TBT 510 ms (performance score 0.23); trace corroborates 4.21 s LCP and two long tasks in a separate run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reserve layout space, defer non-critical modules/media, and measure each representative template against CWV budgets.

findings.summary: The unauthenticated landing page ships a very heavy dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR captures 159 requests and 6,436,533 transferred bytes, including 78 scripts (2.90 MB), 45 images (2.46 MB) and 4 media requests (820 KB).
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the unauthenticated critical graph, lazy-load below-fold and auth dependencies, and avoid loading video until it provides visible user value.

findings.summary: JavaScript dominates the initial load.
findings.evidence: HAR records 78 script requests and 2.90 MB script transfer; Lighthouse identifies large first-party bundles and missing/403 source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Run route-level coverage, split unauth landing/auth code, remove duplicate dependencies, and serve usable source maps to authorised tooling.

findings.summary: Reflow and touch target accessibility fail on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360 px screenshot is clipped with 569 px horizontal overflow and Lighthouse fails the target-size audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow 320 px reflow without two-dimensional scrolling and enlarge/space interactive targets.

findings.summary: The page logs avoidable runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records a FedCM NetworkError and two first-party 404 requests during load; HAR confirms 404 responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle expected identity-provider states without console errors and fix or suppress invalid first-party requests.

findings.summary: Image delivery lacks robust sizing and responsive optimisation.
findings.evidence: The image probe reports 36/36 images without width/height, 27 oversized, 35 below-fold not lazy, 11 without srcset and no modern-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load non-LCP images and negotiate AVIF/WebP where quality allows.

findings.summary: Browser platform hygiene has measurable regressions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a BFCache blocker and missing/403 source maps for large first-party modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the BFCache blocker and make production source maps available to authorised diagnostics or stop advertising inaccessible map URLs.

findings.summary: The India homepage publishes an invalid cross-locale canonical.
findings.evidence: The live DOM canonical is https://www.pinterest.com/ while the audited URL is https://in.pinterest.com/; Lighthouse fails the canonical audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid self/locale canonical consistent with hreflang and sitemap signals.

findings.summary: The homepage core content is effectively a JavaScript shell for non-JS crawlers.
findings.evidence: Discoverability reports 1% rendered-word coverage, isJsShell:true and no raw-HTML h1; the crawler screenshot contains almost no core content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful homepage headings, copy and crawlable discovery links, then progressively enhance.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP posture is weaker than the transport baseline.
findings.evidence: Cookies audit finds five cookies flagged insecure, including non-Secure g_state, _b and _routing_id and multiple SameSite=None cookies; CSP permits unsafe-inline and Permissions-Policy is missing. No client secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, narrow SameSite=None to justified cases, remove unsafe-inline where nonce/strict-dynamic can cover scripts/styles, and define Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Substantial tracking and third-party activity occurs on the initial experience.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence finds nine third-party origins and Pinterest tracker endpoints; HAR attributes 137/159 requests and 6.28 MB to cross-origin hosts before consent was acted on.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics behind consent, minimise unauthenticated telemetry, batch necessary events and document each third party.

findings.summary: The observed login surface does not offer phishing-resistant authentication.
findings.evidence: Login exposes email/password and Google/QR options; no passkey/WebAuthn affordance was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey sign-in and registration alongside recovery-safe alternatives, with conditional UI where supported.

findings.summary: The homepage does not progressively expose its core discovery content.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML is 1.1 MB yet contains only 7 content tokens and 1% of rendered words; without JavaScript the homepage is a shell. A board detail fares better at 57%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the public discovery shell and key links/content, then hydrate enhancements without replacing the usable baseline.

findings.summary: HTTP failures do not lead to intentional recovery UI.
findings.evidence: The synthetic missing route shows the normal homepage and HAR records failed first-party calls without a visible recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use correct HTTP statuses and dedicated empty/error states with retry, back and home actions.

findings.summary: The login form did not expose visible empty-submit guidance in the exercised state.
findings.evidence: After requestSubmit() with empty email and password, the captured form remains visually unchanged with no clear inline error or recovery instruction.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, focus the first invalid field and announce concise errors with an aria-live summary.

findings.summary: The media payload is disproportionate for the first unauthenticated viewport.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 2.46 MB of images and 820 KB of media; image audit finds 27 oversized and zero modern-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP responsive images and defer below-fold/video resources until needed.

findings.summary: Initial background work and fetching are excessive.
findings.evidence: The landing page performs 159 requests, including 78 scripts and 19 fetch/XHR requests, while Lighthouse reaches only 0.23 performance.
findings.suggestedFix: Budget unauthenticated work, conditionally load auth/analytics modules, and deprioritise background fetches.

findings.summary: The baseline memory footprint is high for an unauthenticated landing page.
findings.evidence: Heap summary contains about 1.12 million V8 snapshot nodes and 71.4 MB self size; runtime reports 56.0 MB used JS heap and 1,294 DOM elements. Repeated scroll did not increase total self size.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce module/object populations on the public shell and track a retained-heap budget per route.

taskList.title: Meet CWV and public-shell payload budgets
Server-render the public discovery shell and correct canonical/error statuses
Harden cookie, CSP, permission and consent-gated telemetry posture
Improve keyboard focus, auth and humane form recovery
Add preference-aware theme and continuity cues
Eliminate runtime/platform errors and fix image delivery
